stem: A client with type 2 diabetes completed diabetes self-management education several years ago. The client is now being discharged after a hospitalization with a new insulin regimen and says, “I already had diabetes education when I was diagnosed.” Which nursing response is best?

options.A: A new referral for diabetes self-management education and support is appropriate because major treatment and care transitions are critical times to reassess education and support needs.
options.B: Repeat DSMES is unnecessary because evidence-based diabetes education is intended to occur only once at diagnosis.
options.C: DSMES should be repeated only if the client specifically requests printed educational materials.
options.D: A new insulin regimen does not change self-management needs, so prior education should be considered permanently sufficient.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend DSMES at diagnosis, annually and/or when treatment goals are not being met, when complicating factors develop, and when transitions in life and care occur. A hospital discharge with a new insulin regimen represents a meaningful treatment and care transition that can change self-management skills and support needs. B and D incorrectly treat education as a one-time event. C is too narrow because DSMES is an interactive, person-centered process that includes problem-solving and behavior support rather than only printed information or client-initiated requests.
educational_objective: Recognize that DSMES is an ongoing process and should be reassessed and provided at critical times such as diagnosis, unmet goals, new complicating factors, and major transitions in treatment or care.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: DSMES Recommendation 5.2 and accompanying text — provide DSMES at diagnosis, annually and/or when not meeting treatment goals, when complicating factors develop, and when transitions in life and care occur; DSMES is an ongoing person-centered process
source_claim_supported: Current ADA standards treat DSMES as ongoing support that should be revisited at defined critical times, including major treatment and care transitions rather than only at initial diagnosis.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate discharge planning, referrals, client education, and continuity of care during transitions
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — DSMES referral during transition to a new insulin regimen
correction_summary: Converted the source timing-recall item into a discharge-transition scenario so it tests application rather than memorization and avoids duplicating V2-Q1447’s initial-diagnosis referral construct. The exact ADA 2026 critical-time recommendations are preserved without adding a fixed session count or schedule.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Recommendation 5.2 and DSMES explanatory text.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: The stem creates a treatment transition with a new insulin regimen. A directly applies the current DSMES timing recommendation without assuming a particular education frequency beyond the guideline.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; a major treatment/care transition is a recommended point to reassess and provide DSMES.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; DSMES is not a one-time diagnosis-only intervention.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; DSMES is broader than printed materials and does not depend solely on the client asking for it.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; a new insulin regimen can materially change self-management tasks and education needs.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A applies the current critical-time framework to the stated transition.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address whether and why DSMES should be repeated in this scenario.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care fits because the nurse is coordinating education and continuity during discharge and treatment transition.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked exact critical-time wording, annual-versus-transition nuance, new-insulin self-management relevance, overlap with Q1447, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
